request.systemPrompt:
You are a software architect performing impact analysis on an existing URL
shortener codebase before a requirement is implemented. You are given a file
inventory of the target service and the contents of files that plausibly relate
to the requirement.

Determine for yourself, from the evidence you were given, whether this
requirement is greenfield (no existing code in the inventory addresses it, so the
impact is on files that do not exist yet) or brownfield (existing code is
directly affected). State which one you concluded and why. Never assume; if the
inventory shows no related files, say plainly that the impact is on new files
that do not exist yet, rather than returning an empty impact.

Respond with exactly one fenced json block containing an object with these keys:
- natureOfChange: string, either "greenfield" or "brownfield", with your
  reasoning folded into the surrounding fields, not asserted without support
- affectedFiles: array of strings, relative paths of existing files this change
  affects, or an empty array if none exist yet
- newFilesExpected: array of strings, relative paths of files that will need to
  be created, for a greenfield change
- affectedApiContracts: array of strings, describing any REST endpoints affected
- affectedDataFlows: array of strings, describing how data moves through the
  affected area
- blastRadius: string, a short assessment of how contained or far-reaching this
  change is
- regressionRisks: array of strings, specific existing behavior that could break

response.text:
```json
{
  "natureOfChange": "brownfield",
  "reasoning": "The codebase already has a well-established URL lookup path (UrlService.findByShortCode, UrlApiController.lookup, UrlRepository.findByShortCode). The new preview endpoint reuses that same lookup path and extends it by fetching the target page's HTML to extract <title> and <meta name='description'> content. The controller, service, and a new response DTO are the primary touch-points; the domain entity and repository are untouched. Because the preview logic (HTTP fetching + HTML parsing) is genuinely new code, at least one new file is expected, but the change lands squarely inside existing packages and wires into existing infrastructure.",
  "affectedFiles": [
    "src/main/java/com/schwab/urlshortener/url/UrlApiController.java",

    "src/test/java/com/schwab/urlshortener/url/UrlServiceIntegrationTest.java",
    "build.gradle.kts"
  ],
  "newFilesExpected": [
    "src/main/java/com/schwab/urlshortener/url/PreviewResponse.java",
    "src/main/java/com/schwab/urlshortener/url/LinkPreviewService.java",
    "src/test/java/com/schwab/urlshortener/url/LinkPreviewServiceTest.java"
  ],
  "affectedApiContracts": [
    "GET /api/urls/{shortCode}/preview — new endpoint returning JSON with at minimum 'title' and 'description' fields scraped from the resolved long URL's HTML"
  ],
  "affectedDataFlows": [
    "Client → GET /api/urls/{shortCode}/preview → UrlApiController → UrlService.findByShortCode (reads DB via UrlRepository) → LinkPreviewService fetches longUrl over HTTP → parses HTML for <title> and <meta name='description'> → PreviewResponse returned to client",
    "The redirect path (RedirectController GET /{shortCode}) is read-only and unaffected, but shares UrlService; any latency or error introduced by the preview path does not touch it"
  ],
  "blastRadius": "Moderately contained. The change adds one new endpoint and one new service class within the existing url package. Existing create, lookup, and redirect flows are not structurally modified. The main risk surface is the outbound HTTP call introduced by LinkPreviewService, which brings in network I/O, timeout configuration, and a potential new library dependency (e.g., Jsoup for HTML parsing), all of which are new to the codebase.",

    "UrlService is shared between the preview and existing flows; any changes made to it (e.g., adding an overloaded method or modifying transaction semantics) could inadvertently affect UrlApiController.lookup and RedirectController.redirect",

}
```
